leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now, and one is scheduled to open tomorrow afternoon with zero margin. The moment Pinckert lands, the balance goes negative by precisely the amount Lokonga's sale returns — not a euro more or less — and a negative balance when the matchday starts scores nothing for the entire matchday. That risk outranks everything else on this page. Two things follow. First, tonight's value tick is a hard checkpoint: it happens before the auction resolves, and if the funding player's value falls the offer must be lowered by at least the drop before it settles, not abandoned. Second, the keeper swap stays off the table while this is live. It was re-costed this run with current figures rather than last run's estimates and the margin is now several times better than when it was withdrawn — but the double structure needs two auctions won and two manual sales executed across three days while Georg is away, at a peak exposure of roughly a quarter of the squad's value, to gain a small handful of points. The break-even failure probability works out at well under two per cent, and the chance of one manual sale being missed over that window is plainly higher, so the answer is no on expected value and not on nerve. It becomes live only if Pinckert is lost — then it is one buy funded by one sale, with the keeper who must land first because he is the only one in the squad.

binding_gap: The binding gap is not a position, it is a body. At eleven players there is no bench, so every knock is fielded and every sale is blocked, and that is what caps the squad's ceiling far more than any individual slot. The twelfth body is the Pinckert purchase, and until it lands nothing else can move: the squad cannot sell an injured full-back, cannot rotate around a doubtful midfielder, and cannot take a cheap upgrade anywhere on the pitch. Within the eleven, the weakest fielded slots are the injured full-back and the doubtful midfielder, and Pinckert replaces the worse of the two contributions. The keeper slot is a real but secondary upgrade worth a fraction of that, and it is deliberately not being pursued while the defender bid is live.

verdict.headline: Hold the line.
verdict.detail: Hold the line. The Pinckert bid is live, uncontested and sitting exactly on the ceiling, and it is the only action that matters between now and the lock — do not raise it (there is nothing left to raise with) and do not abandon it. Nothing new on the board this run beats it: the two genuinely new listings of consequence are a returning Musiala who is still a substitute, and a Dortmund defender who limped off on Saturday. The one mandatory checkpoint is tonight's market-value tick, which lands before the auction resolves: the Lokonga sale that unwinds this purchase clears the negative balance to exactly zero, with no margin at all, so if his value falls tonight the offer has to come down by at least the drop tomorrow morning. Everything else this run is bookkeeping and two pieces of squad news.

sell.reason: One sale, conditional, and its justification has changed even though the answer has not. Lokonga is the funding leg for Pinckert and nothing else can play that role — Conte's value falls short of what the purchase needs, so substituting him leaves the balance negative at the lock and forfeits the entire matchday. The sale must happen only AFTER Pinckert actually lands; if that auction is lost, the sale is void, the squad stays at eleven and the shape stays legal. What changed: the previous run sold him on availability, on the ground that nobody would say when his back would be right. A dated Ligainsider item and Polzin's own quotes, both from today, now expect him available for Leipzig. That does not rescue him — the sale was never worth making on fitness. He is the second-worst outfielder in the squad and the trade buys a defender with three times his scoring rate. Selling him is a points decision now, not an injury decision, and a future run meeting the return news should not reverse it on that basis. Widmer is the other sale that wants making and cannot be made: he now carries a dated knee entry, he was left out of the Mainz eleven, and both his substitute appearances add up to less than half a game — but selling him at a squad of eleven drops it to ten and the under-eleven penalty costs far more than he does. He stays a designated sale for the moment a thirteenth body exists, not a twelfth. Do not buy a cheap zero-point body to enable it; that route was costed this run and comes out clearly worse than simply selling Lokonga and buying Pinckert.
